contract:
## Shared Types
- `Tile`: `{ row: number, col: number, type: number }` (same shape as in `game.js`)
- `Board`: class in `game.js` with methods `remove(row, col)`, `getTile(row, col)`, `isCleared()`
- `Path` result: `Array<{row: number, col: number}> | null`
- `EventBus`: class exported from `eventBus.js` with `on(event, callback)` and `emit(event, data)`. Singleton instance `bus`.
- Constants: `CELL_SIZE = 60` (used for coordinate calculations)

## API Contract
- Event names (all modules use these exact strings):
  - `'match'` – emitted when two tiles are successfully removed. Data: `{ tile1: Tile, tile2: Tile }`
  - `'invalid'` – emitted on an invalid attempt. Data: `{}`
  - `'start'` – emitted once on the first match of the game. Data: `{}`
  - `'gameOver'` – emitted when the board is cleared. Data: `{}`
- Module initialization signatures:
  - `ui.initGame(svgElement, scoreElement, bus)` – must attach click handlers, use `bus` to emit events.
  - `sound.initSound(bus)` – subscribes to events and plays `<audio>` by id.
  - `particles.initParticles(bus, container)` – subscribes to `'match'` and creates particle effects inside `container`.
  - `background.applyBackground(container)` – sets the background image of `container`.
- Rendering calls (available from `renderer.js`):
  - `renderer.createBoardSvg(board, svgElement)` – redraws the board
  - `renderer.animatePath(svg, path, onComplete)` – animates a connection line
- Board manipulation (available from `game.js`):
  - `board.remove(row, col)` – removes a tile from the grid
  - `PathFinder.findPath(board, start, end)` – returns path or `null`

## Naming Conventions
- DOM IDs:
  - `game-board` – the SVG element for the board
  - `score` – the score display element
  - `sound-match`, `sound-invalid`, `sound-start`, `sound-win` – `<audio>` elements
  - `particles-layer` – overlay container for particle effects
  - `background-container` – container for the background image
- File paths:
  - JavaScript modules are at the project root: `game.js`, `renderer.js`, `ui.js`, `main.js`, `eventBus.js`, `sound.js`, `particles.js`, `background.js`.
  - Audio assets: `static/sounds/match.mp3`, `static/sounds/invalid.mp3`, `static/sounds/start.mp3`, `static/sounds/win.mp3`.
  - Background image: `static/bg.jpg` (generated by `background_generator.py`).

subtasks.task: Fix tile elimination and expose match callbacks so that a user can click two tiles, see them removed, and win the game.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking two tiles of the same type with a valid connecting path removes both tiles from the board and SVG immediately.
Clicking two tiles that cannot be connected (different types or blocked path) has no visual effect (tiles remain) and emits an `invalid` event.
When all tiles are cleared, a victory message (e.g., score display change) is shown and a `gameOver` event is emitted.
The first successful match of a game session emits a `start` event.
Every successful match emits a `match` event with `{ tile1, tile2 }` on the shared event bus.
The game board is correctly redrawn after each match (no leftover tiles, remainders keep correct positions).

subtasks.task: Add sound effects so the user hears audio feedback for match, invalid attempt, start, and win.
acceptance_criteria: An `<audio>` element with id `sound-match` plays a distinct sound every time a `match` event is emitted.
An `<audio>` element with id `sound-invalid` plays a sound on the `invalid` event.
An `<audio>` element with id `sound-start` plays a sound once on the `start` event.
An `<audio>` element with id `sound-win` plays a sound on the `gameOver` event.
Audio files exist at `static/sounds/match.mp3`, `static/sounds/invalid.mp3`, `static/sounds/start.mp3`, `static/sounds/win.mp3` and are playable.
No JavaScript errors in the console; sounds do not block the game loop.

subtasks.task: Enhance visual appeal by adding particle animations on match and richer tile designs so the game looks polished.
acceptance_criteria: Tiles use a more vibrant color palette with at least 4 distinct types, each including decorative SVG details (e.g., inner shapes, gradients, shadows).
When a `match` event occurs, a burst of animated particles (confetti/dots) appears centered between the two matched tiles, expands, fades out, and is removed from the DOM.
Particles are rendered inside a `div#particles-layer` overlay that is positioned on top of the game board.
The board redraw still works correctly after the renderer changes; no tiles are misaligned.
Animation runs smoothly (no noticeable jank on boards up to 8x10).

subtasks.task: Integrate a beautiful background image so the game feels warm and aesthetically pleasing.
acceptance_criteria: A background image based on a warm gradient (or API-generated) is displayed behind the entire game area.
The image is loaded from `static/bg.jpg` (or another path if specified).
The background does not obscure the board – tiles remain clearly visible.
The `background_generator.py` script, when run, produces `static/bg.jpg` (update the generator if a real API key is provided; otherwise keep the gradient mock).
The background is applied via the `applyBackground(container)` function and does not cause layout shifts.

subtasks.task: Wire all components together so the full game runs with sounds, particles, background, and correct elimination.
acceptance_criteria: `index.html` contains `<audio>` elements with ids `sound-match`, `sound-invalid`, `sound-start`, `sound-win`, and includes `src` attributes pointing to the correct `static/sounds/` files.

`index.html` contains a `
` overlay placed exactly over the game board, and a `
` covering the viewport.
`main.js` imports `initGame` from `./ui.js`, `initSound` from `./sound.js`, `initParticles` from `./particles.js`, `applyBackground` from `./background.js`, and `bus` from `./eventBus.js`.

In `main.js`, after `DOMContentLoaded`, calls `applyBackground(document.getElementById('background-container'))`, then `initGame(svg, score, bus)`, then `initSound(bus)`, then `initParticles(bus, document.getElementById('particles-layer'))` – in that order.
The game loads in a browser without any errors; all interactive features (click, match, elimination, sound, particles, background) work together.
When the board is cleared, the win sound plays and a victory indication (score update or message) appears.
